items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: He was a friend of mine. He told me whenever you need something, just wire it.

ctx.x: That's what happened in New York. This double-crossing and this Al Travis stealing everything he could. Booking my band five and six nights. Five and six different towns on the same nights. But he was getting deposits off of all of them. We weren't seeing the deposits. We played one town. A lot of people were looking for us. We didn't show up there when we got a lawsuit through the union.
We once talked about being stranded. If you did lose all your money and all that. There was a German man you would wire for money?

No, I know what you're referring to. This was in Texas. That was in East Bernard. I can't recall his name right now. But not being stranded. He was a friend of mine. He told me whenever you need something, just wire it. But now the time that I actually was stranded was when I was with this Chauncey Holland or Al Travis I think. It was in a little town in Carbondale, Illinois. And there was an old lady there, another lady. She liked me and she liked the band. So we were living with her and we didn't have another…
